items.title: 68359_Zutty Singleton oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] This is after he and James P. had got drunk was it? [INTERVIEWEE] Yes.

ctx.x: Yes. So that's where that Viva La France came from. (LAUGHTER). Old Tommy looked at Pandssie and say, and he had on a cap and it was cold, he said, 'Viva La France. Because he know that would get that Frenchman's see? So, Pandssie was still looking sad and Tommy said, 'Viva La France I say.' And Pandssie kind of smiled a little and Tommy said, well alright then God damn it.
This is after he and James P. had got drunk was it?

items.title: 68359_Zutty Singleton oral history interview
items.q: Because she was singing that James P. Johnson, 'Charleston, Charleston.'

ctx.x: Did you say that it was Ethel Walters that taught you the Charleston?

Yes indeed. She sure did. Because she was singing that James P. Johnson, 'Charleston, Charleston.' You know she'd get right, I was down in the pit, but she was up on the stage and she would (SOUND OF CLAPPING). But I couldn't make it with two in a bar. So when I put that four in a bar that made that Charleston. I could make it with that. Yes. And Tim Moore, he was on circuit then. Him and a midget used to have a prize fight. They had a little scene in there where he and this midget would fight like. And this…
